justification: Attacks the skill-promotion step of self-evolving skill systems (inclusion/attribution/realization), so the object is the outer evolution loop; evidence is lab trials at varied attacker-support ratios across six evolvers.

Contribution is the Pask system's hybrid workspace/user/global long-term memory for grounding proactive action; evaluated only on the authors' LatentNeeds-Bench under latency constraints, i.e. lab validation.

Claim is a fixed-weight self-evolving runtime that admits memories, skills and verifiers into persistent state between missions; headline evidence is seven benchmark arenas (SWE-Bench Pro, AARRI-Bench), not field study.

Contribution is state-aware routing among context-management strategies (what history is kept) rather than candidate solutions; validated on web-agent benchmarks across backbones. Runner-up: deliberative_search for the parallel branches.
CAT makes context maintenance a callable tool with structured workspace and milestone compression; validated in the lab on SWE-Bench-Verified against ReAct and static-compression baselines.

MOSS's claim is a dynamic context-management runtime keeping Python context and local-variable isolation across turns; support is 'a series of case studies' showing framework use, with no measured validation.

Reframes GUI interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context is retained or discarded; evidence is AndroidWorld plus an extended long-horizon suite, a lab benchmark run.

Contribution is three context-efficiency mechanisms (LoRA-distilled context state object, compact tool schemas, JIT schema passing); evaluated by comparing a 3B agent against a conventional baseline on user tasks, not a named benchmark.

VISTA is a plug-in layer exposing typed context blocks, token usage and remaining budget so the agent makes keep-or-archive decisions; lab evidence on LOCA-Bench, BrowseComp-Plus and GAIA with ablations.
Scroll is a context manager with append-only event log, typed kernel namespace and recoverable eviction deciding what enters the working view; validated on LongMemEval_S, BEAM_10M and LOCA_256K.

Integrates a risk encoder over time into a continuous escalation-pressure signal that governs when the agent defers to a clinician; evidence is synthetic ward scenarios comparing stateless, first- and second-order dynamics.

Empirical audit of one named mechanism - agent context management - comparing observation masking, LLM summarization and a new hybrid; evidence is SWE-bench Verified across five model configurations in the lab.

BACM formulates when and how much interaction history to compress as a budget-constrained sequential decision, learned by RL; validated on multi-objective QA and web-browsing benchmarks. Runner-up: budget_and_termination_control.

The stated contribution is a measurement and stress-test framework (replay pairing, hidden-state probe, strict stripping) for whether plans persist; evidence is paired with/without-plan trajectory runs, a lab design.
CAT makes context maintenance a callable tool with structured workspace and milestone compression; validated in the lab on SWE-Bench-Verified against ReAct and static-compression baselines.
CoMem decouples memory summarization from the agent loop via a k-step-off asynchronous pipeline with reward-aligned training; lab evidence is latency and accuracy on SWE-Bench-Verified.

Empirical audit of process verification as an acceptance judgement on intermediate MAS steps (judges, reward models, PRMs at two granularities); evidence is runs over six MAS frameworks on reasoning benchmarks in the lab.

GCC turns agent context into a persistent navigable workspace with COMMIT/BRANCH/MERGE/CONTEXT for checkpointing and hierarchical retrieval; validated on SWE-Bench Verified and BrowseComp. Runner-up: planning_and_control_flow.

Contribution shapes evolutionary search over candidates - momentum-based backtracking against mode collapse and a sampling policy unifying backtracking with cross-trajectory crossover; validated on LLM-SR, KernelBench, Modded NanoGPT.

Headline artefact is LoCoEval, a benchmark instrument for repository-oriented long-horizon context management, generalising past any one mechanism; 7 baselines and 3 backbones are run on it in the lab.

FormalAgentLib formally verifies workflow semantic consistency in Lean4 and localises trajectory failures, a proof-based check that gates which workflows stand; validated on SWE-Bench-Verified hard subset and ELAIP-Bench over 5 LLMs.

ACE is a plug-in module assigning each historical step a raw/abstract/drop type with lossless recovery, governing what state carries forward; validated by attaching it to four agent frameworks and comparing on benchmarks.

HyMem separates context into functional layers so execution traces do not pollute the persistent planning context, with summaries kept across refreshes; lab evidence is Pass@1 on GAIA and BrowseComp-plus.

Reframes GUI interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context is retained or discarded; evidence is AndroidWorld plus an extended long-horizon suite, a lab benchmark run.

Lead contribution is a symbolic action protocol partitioning behaviour into planning, task-solving and retrospection with deterministic execution format that fixes the next step; validated on multi-hop QA with Qwen2.5/3 models.
